title: A Dataset and a Technique for Generalized Nuclear Segmentation for Computational Pathology

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Nuclear segmentation in digital microscopic tissue images can enable extraction of high-quality features for nuclear morphometrics and other analysis in computational pathology.

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】However, training machine learning algorithms requires data sets of images, in which a vast number of nuclei have been annotated.

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】Because our data set is taken from multiple hospitals and includes a diversity of nuclear appearances from several patients, disease states, and organs, techniques trained on it are likely to generalize well and work right out-of-the-box on other H&E-stained images.

evidence.text: However, training machine learning algorithms requires data sets of images, in which a vast number of nuclei have been annotated.

Because our data set is taken from multiple hospitals and includes a diversity of nuclear appearances from several patients, disease states, and organs, techniques trained on it are likely to generalize well and work right out-of-the-box on other H&E-stained images.
